cards.explanation: The answer is men from thirty to fifty years old. That's the range the LORD gives Moses and Aaron for everyone qualified to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 4:3). It comes up again for each clan, so it's no accident. If somebody asked me my age to get in, I'd have nothing to say, because I don't have one.

The answer is carrying. First Aaron and his sons cover the holy objects, and only then do the Kohathites come and do the carrying (Numbers 4:15). One group wraps and another group hauls. In my bakery I do both jobs with one mustache, and you can tell by the boxes.

The answer is False, and the text is plain about it. “But they must not touch the holy objects, or they will die.” (Numbers 4:15). Being careful isn't part of the verse at all. Aaron and his sons cover the holy objects first, and only then do the Kohathites come to carry (Numbers 4:15).

The answer is the entire tabernacle and everything in it. Eleazar, Aaron's son, who served as a priest (Numbers 3:4), has oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy objects and their utensils (Numbers 4:16). The oil, the incense and the grain offering are only part of his job. That's a lot to keep track of, friends. I can barely keep track of one apron.

The answer is that Aaron and his sons go in and assign each man his task. They assign each man his task and what he is to carry (Numbers 4:19). The LORD gives this so the Kohathites may live and not die when they come near the most holy things. Nobody has to guess what to grab. It's like a boss who hands out the jobs before anybody picks up anything.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “But the Kohathites are not to go in and look at the holy objects, even for a moment, or they will die.” (Numbers 4:20). That's a serious line, and it's meant to be. It also sits right beside the LORD's care for them, because He had just said He wants them to live and not die when they come near the most holy things (Numbers 4:19).

The answer is the curtains and coverings. The Gershonites carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering of fine leather, the entrance curtains and the courtyard curtains (Numbers 4:25-26). Their ropes and equipment go along too. That's a whole lot of fabric, friends. I'd be lost in the first fold.

The answer is False. All the Gershonites' service is done at the direction of Aaron and his sons (Numbers 4:27). The LORD tells Moses, “you are to assign to them all that they are responsible to carry.” Nobody gets to grab the lightest curtain and run. I'd have been first in line for that, no question.

The answer is the frames and posts. The Merarites carry the frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts and bases. They also carry the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs and ropes (Numbers 4:31-32). Every piece matters when a tent has to go up again. I lose a single pen in a junk drawer, so I'd never survive this job.

The answer is that each item is assigned by name. The LORD says, “You shall assign by name the items that they are responsible to carry.” (Numbers 4:32). With that many pieces, I think assigning by name keeps everybody clear on what's theirs. I wish my kitchen drawers ran like that.

The answer is True. Ithamar, Aaron's son, who served as a priest (Numbers 3:4), directs both clans. The Gershonites' duties are under his direction (Numbers 4:28), and so is the work of the Merarites (Numbers 4:33). One director, two clans. That's a big stack of tent gear for one man to keep track of.

The answer is False, and verse 49 is why. After the count of 8,580, each man is assigned his work and burden, so it reaches the Gershonites and the Merarites too (Numbers 4:46-49). Three clans, three sets of jobs, and every counted man gets his own assignment. That's a whole lot of names on one list, friends. I'd need a bigger apron just to carry the paperwork.
